text:
B: Here we go, can you hear me alright, mate?
A: Yeah. Yeah, fine.
B: Sound. I'm Ryan, I'm in Stockport. Well, I work in Manchester, but I'm kipping in Stockport, do you know what I mean.
A: Gareth. Basingstoke.
B: Basingstoke! Never been. I've been through it on the train, I think. Is it all roundabouts? Someone told me it's all roundabouts.
A: Er, there's a few, yeah. It's sort of known for that.
B: Ha, I knew it. Here, how'd you get on with that puzzle thing at the start? I was flying for the first bit, then the one with the shapes, the rotating ones, I just sat there, mate, I just stared at it. I reckon I guessed the last three.
A: Er, that one was alright actually. It's kind of what I do all day.
B: Go on then, what do you do?
A: Structural engineer. Warehouses mostly, retail units. Working out if the steel's big enough, basically.
B: That's a proper job, that. That's the one where if you get it wrong the roof comes in, isn't it?
A: Pretty much, yeah.
B: No pressure then. I run a bar, me, music venue in the Northern Quarter. So if I get it wrong, the worst that happens is a band turns up and there's no lager, which, to be fair, is nearly as bad. I've got about eighteen staff, I do the booking, licensing, all that. Love it, honestly, apart from the spreadsheets. The owners want everything on a spreadsheet. I'm like, mate, it's a bar, just come in on a Friday and look, it's rammed.
A: Yeah. I'm not great on the admin side either.
B: Are you not? See, I'd have had you down as a spreadsheet man.
A: Calcs, yeah. Timesheets, no. They go in late every month.
B: Ha! There you go, we'd get on. Here, what's on your fridge there, is that a Saints magnet?
A: Yeah, fixtures. Southampton. My dad's lot, so I didn't really get a choice.
B: Same with me and County. Stockport County, season ticket, Edgeley Park, I take my nephew. He's twelve, he's just got into it properly this year and now he knows more than me, it's doing my head in. He's correcting me on stats in the car.
A: My lad's fifteen. We go to St Mary's a couple of times a season.
B: That's good, that. Is he into it?
A: Er, yeah, when he's not on his phone. He should be revising, GCSE year next year. He says he is.
B: He's not.
A: No, he's not.
B: Ha! I wasn't either. I left uni after a year, so I'm not the one to ask, but you turned out alright, didn't you, with the steel and that. Do you still play at all? I do five-a-side Wednesdays and I've got into padel, have you tried padel? It's like tennis but in a cage, it's mint, honestly, I'm obsessed.
A: No. I did five-a-side till my late thirties. Group sort of drifted off.
B: You want to get back into it, mate. Or padel, padel's easier on the knees.
A: Maybe. I walk the dog mostly. Bonnie. That's about it.
B: That counts. My sister's got a dog, she walks it in the rain at six in the morning, she's a machine. I'm at her place at the minute actually, spare room, long story.
A: Right. Yeah.
B: Bit embarrassing at thirty-seven, but she does a cracking tea, so I'm not complaining. Do you do the cooking, or—
A: Yeah, me. Spag bol, chilli. Friday's takeaway, that's the highlight, to be honest.
B: Friday takeaway's sacred. What do you go for, Chinese?
A: Usually, yeah. Or a Domino's if the kids win.
B: Oh, you've got to come up to Manchester, mate, there's this Vietnamese place round the corner from work, I'm telling you—
